rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because night vigil is exceptionally meritorious, God emphasizes its demands to encourage the worshipper to pursue the best worship.
rows.anchor: ولما أفهم هذا أن التهجد في غاية العظمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naashi'at are the night’s successive hours, when worship begins lightly as a vigorous person rises from bed with strong resolve.
rows.anchor: أي ساعاته التي كل واحدة منها ناشئة والعبادة تنشأ فيه بغاية الخفة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the period after the night prayer is naashi'ah, while the period before it is not.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : ما كان بعد العشاء فهو ناشئة

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha identifies naashi'ah as rising for worship after sleep.
rows.anchor: وقالت عائشة رضي الله عنها

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Azhari glosses naashi'ah as standing in prayer, a verbal noun on the pattern of aafiyah, meaning pardon.
rows.anchor: الأزهري : الناشئة القيام , مصدر جاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night vigil is more burdensome and weighty because it gives up rest and beloved habits; it also conveys firmness.
rows.anchor: أشد } أي أثقل وأقوى وأمتن وأرصن

rows.speaker: الجماعة
rows.claim: The general reading has waṭʾan, a verbal noun from waṭiʾa, and the commentary associates it with firmness of footing.
rows.anchor: على أنه مصرد وطئ في قراءة الجماعة

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وابن عامر
rows.claim: Abu Amr and Ibn Amir read wiṭāʾan, from wāṭāʾa, for accord between heart and tongue and submission; the author calls this reciprocal form more emphatic.
rows.anchor: على أنه مصدر واطأ مثل قاتل على قراءة أبي عمرو وابن عامر بالكسر والمد وهي أبلغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night speech is more sound in understanding and more affecting on hearts because the heart is present, sounds are quiet, blessings descend, and ostentation is less likely.
rows.anchor: وأعظم سدادا من جهة القيل في فهمه ووقعه في القلوب بحضور القلب ورياقة الليل بهدوء الأصواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night worship is paired with daytime livelihood: earning provision supports religious duties and dependents without laziness, weariness, or excess.
rows.anchor: مبينا ما به صلاح الدنيا التي هي فيها المعاش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address may be to any night worshipper or specifically the Prophet; addressing him would strengthen the obligation for the community.
rows.anchor: أي أيها المتهجد أو يا أكرم العباد غن كان الخطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ليكون آكد في إلزام الأمة به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Daytime activity is extended movement and turning about; a diligent person seems to swim freely through unobstructed space.
rows.anchor: حتى يكون كأنه لشدة عزمه وسرعة حركته كالسابح فيما لا عائق له فيه

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawi says the root sense of sabḥ is going quickly.
rows.anchor: قال البغوي : وأصل السبح سرعة الذهاب

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi explains sabḥ as ease of movement.
rows.anchor: وقال الرازي : سهولة الحركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remember God by every form of remembrance, including praise, submission, prayer, recitation, supplication, and pursuing religious learning and proper conduct; persist in it.
rows.anchor: بكل ما يكون ذكرا من اسم وصفة وثناء وخضوع وتسبيح وتحميد وصلاة وقراءة ودعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Magnifying God's name magnifies the One named through monotheism and sincerity, helping the servant in both the present and future lives.
rows.anchor: فإذا عظمت الاسم بالذكر فقد عظمت المسمى بالتوحيد والإخلاص , وذلك عون لك على مصالح الدارين

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When Fatima asked for a servant to spare her fatigue, the Prophet directed her to glorify, praise, and magnify God at bedtime.
rows.anchor: أرشد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أعز الخلق عليه فاطمة ابنته رضي الله عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabattul means progressively cutting oneself off from distractions and making all acts sincere for God until detachment becomes a settled disposition.
rows.anchor: اجتهد في قطع نفسك عن كل شاغل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root batl means cutting; a batlah charity is separated from its giver.
rows.anchor: وهو من البتل وهو القطع

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam defines tabattul as rejecting the world and seeking what is with God.
rows.anchor: قال زيد بن أسلم : التبتل رفض الدنيا وما فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maryam is called al-Batul for turning away from all creation toward God; Fatima is likewise called al-Batul as cut off from any peer or equal.
rows.anchor: والبتول مريم عليها السلام لانقطاعها إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse calls for the stance of the testimony of divine unity: turn to God, turn away from all else, persist in remembrance, and cast off desire.
rows.anchor: فالمراد بهذا هو المراد بكلمة التوحيد المقتضية للإقبال عليه والإعراض عن كل ما سواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paired forms create rhetorical completion: the verb tabattul implies an omitted verbal noun, while tabtīlan implies an omitted verb, stressing effort and difficulty.
rows.anchor: والآية من الاحتباك وهو ظاهر

rows.speaker: ابن عامر ويعقوب والكوفيون غير حفص
rows.claim: Ibn Amir, Yaqub, and the Kufan readers except Hafs read the following Lord-title in the accusative; the remaining readers use the nominative as an independent exaltation.
rows.anchor: في قراءة ابن عامر ويعقوب والكوفيين غير حفص معظما له بالقطع في قراءة الباقين بالرفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next description of God links remembrance to gratitude: God supplied the night for worship and the day for activity.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الواجب على كل أحد شكر المنعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse teaches moderation in worship to spare people hardship, since life is the opportunity to gather good before death.
rows.anchor: أشار سبحانه وتعالى إلى الاقتصاد تخفيفا لما يلحق الإنسان من النصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul belongs to the subtle, instantly created world of command, while the dense body belongs to the gradual world of creation; the soul is therefore alien to bodily attachments.
rows.anchor: فإن الروح في غاية اللطافة ، والجسد في غاية الكثافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembrance, prayer, and good works help the soul reconnect with its elevated spiritual realm; wisdom means justice and moderation in words and deeds.
rows.anchor: وذلك بصرف القلب كله عن هذه الدنايا والتلبس بالأذكار والصلوات وجميع الأعمال الصالحات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adnā means less in duration here; nearness and lower rank both imply a shorter distance, explaining the word's shared senses.
rows.anchor: لأن كلا منهما يلزم منه قلة المسافة

words: أدنى من ثلثي الليل ونصفه وثلثه
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the general reading, the Prophet stood for less than two-thirds on some nights and less than the half and third on others.
rows.anchor: أدنى من كل منهما في بعض الليالي

rows.speaker: ابن كثير والكوفيون
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir and the Kufan readers put half and third in the accusative, specifying the amounts included under less than two-thirds.
rows.anchor: المعنى على قراءة ابن كثير والكوفيين بالنصب تعيين النصف والثلث الداخل تحت الأدنى من الثلثين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both readings match the earlier choice to pray a full half, less than a half (a third), more than a half (two-thirds), or an even smaller portion (a quarter).
rows.anchor: وهو على القراءتين مطابق لما وقع التخيير فيه في أول السورة بين قيام النصف بتمامه أو الناقص منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ṭāʾifah is a group whose members are suited to gathering around the Prophet and turning toward one another.
rows.anchor: أي يقوم كذلك جماعة يفيها أهليبة التحلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those with the Prophet are his companions in words and deeds, meaning Muslims; the broader phrase avoids implying that those who did not pray were not Muslims.
rows.anchor: وكأنه اختار هذا دون أن يقول من المسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone measures night and day with exact precision and knows every minute because He created them; the verse recalls 67:14.
rows.anchor: فيعلم كل دقيقة منهما على

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knew people could neither calculate the night's measure precisely nor sustain the prescribed practice.
rows.anchor: أي تطيقوا التقدير علما وعملا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said, “Be upright, and you will not encompass it,” cited to illustrate human inability to calculate fully.
rows.anchor: قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم ' استقيموا ولن تحصوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God lifted the earlier obligation of precisely measured night vigil and licensed people to leave it without blame.
rows.anchor: رجع بالنسخ عما كان أوجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the relief repentance does not imply a prior sin; the heavy obligation could have led people into sin.
rows.anchor: وكأنه سماه توبة وإن لم يكن ثم معصية إشارة إلى أنه من شأنه لثقله أن يجر إلى المعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recitation stands for prayer because it is prayer's greatest pillar, indicating that night vigil is recommended rather than obligatory.
rows.anchor: معبرًا عن الصلاة بالقراءة لأنها أعظم أركانها إشارة إلى أن التهجد مستحب لا واجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recite whatever is easy from the Qur'an, in or outside prayer and by night or day.
rows.anchor: أي يفي الصلاة أمو غيرها في الليل والنهار

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri says the easy recitation may be five verses or more.
rows.anchor: قال القشيري : من خمس آيات إلى ما زاد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An unnamed view sets the easy minimum at ten verses or more.
rows.anchor: ويقال : من عشر آيات إلى ما يزيد

rows.speaker: قيس بن أبي حازم
rows.claim: Qays ibn Abi Hazim reports praying behind Ibn Abbas, who recited al-Fatihah and one verse of al-Baqarah in each of the first two units.
rows.anchor: قال قيس بن أبي حازم : صليت خلف ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما بالبصرة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes the command as bare recitation in place of the former night-prayer obligation, as an added easing.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنه أمر بالقراءة مجردة إقامة لها مقام ما كان يجب عليهم من الصلاة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
rows.claim: The Prophet said that praying with ten verses removes heedlessness, one hundred marks devotion, and one thousand brings the rank of the richly rewarded; Abu Dawud, Ibn Khuzaymah, and Ibn Hibban transmit it.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص رضي الله عنهما قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: المنذري
rows.claim: Al-Mundhiri says the thousand verses begin at Surat al-Mulk and continue to the end of the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: قال المنذري : من سورة الملك إلى آخر القرآن ألف آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God spells out why the former night-prayer measure was eased: illness, travel, and fighting make exact observance difficult.
rows.anchor: فسر ذلك العلم المجمل بعلم مفصل بيانا لحكمة أخرى للنسخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the surah is among the earliest revelations, it foretells that the Muslim community will grow greatly.
rows.anchor: وهذه السورة من أول ما أنزل عليه صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Illness is mentioned first as the broadest excuse and one over which the sick person has no control.
rows.anchor: ذكر عذر المريض وبه أنه لكونه أعم ولا قدرة للمريض على دفعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Travelers are described as striking the earth because a diligent walker strikes it with his foot.
rows.anchor: لأن الماشي بجد واجتهاد يضرب الأرض برجله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Travel for trade follows illness as another common reason that prevents exact night observance.
rows.anchor: أتبعه السفر للتجارة لأنه يليه في العموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking God's bounty includes pursuing profit in trade or acquiring knowledge; God's provision exceeds people's hopes.
rows.anchor: من الربح في التجارة أو تعلم العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fighting in God's way means attacking God's enemies; the repeated phrase exalts jihad and avoids confusion with a return to commerce.
rows.anchor: وأظهر ولم يضمر تعظيما للجهاد ولئلا يلبس بالعود إلى المتجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase places the fighting within God's path and removes moral and physical obstacles that block that path.
rows.anchor: ذلك القتل مظروف لطريق الملك الأعظم

words: يضربون في الأرض يبتغون من فضل الله
rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Al-Baghawi transmits Ibn Masud's view that a patient trader who imports goods to a Muslim city and sells at that day's price is ranked with martyrs.
rows.anchor: روى إبراهيم عن ابن مسعود رضي اله عنه

words: يضربون في الأرض يبتغون من فضل الله
rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar says that, after martyrdom, he would prefer to die traveling and seeking God's bounty.
rows.anchor: وعن عبد الله بن عمر رضي الله عنهما أنه قال : ما خلق الله موتة أموتها بعد القتل في سبيل الله أحب إلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These additional excuses explain why God repeats the permission: each person should recite whatever is easy from the same Qur'an.
rows.anchor: رتب عليها الحكم السابق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The required vigil became an easy portion of recitation and was later superseded by the five obligatory prayers.
rows.anchor: فصار الواجب قيام شيء من على وجه التيسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit command to establish prayer either favors understanding the prior recitation as independent of formal prayer or specifies that it meant prayer.
rows.anchor: قال ترجيحا لإرادة هذا الثاني أو تنصيصا على إرادة الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Establish the obligatory prayer with all its pillars, conditions, preliminaries, complements, forms, and refinements.
rows.anchor: الكتوبة بجيمع الأمور التي تقوم بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Give the required zakat from the good wealth God has bestowed; it is the financial pillar alongside prayer.
rows.anchor: من طيب أموالكم التي أنعمنا بها عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The goodly loan includes voluntary acts of charity and worship with body and wealth, offered eagerly and beautifully while healthy and prosperous; God preserves and multiplies it.
rows.anchor: من نوافل الخيرات كلها في جميع شرعه برغبة تامة وعلى هيئة جميلة في ابتدائه وانتهائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general command covers every good deed, bodily or financial, sent ahead for the afterlife when people can no longer act; God preserves it for them.
rows.anchor: من عبادات البدن والمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A separator may occur between the indefinite terms because the comparative form afʿal min functions like a definite expression and does not take the definite article.
rows.anchor: وجاز وقوع الفصل بين غير معرفتين لأن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every good deed is repaid, whether done near death or earlier and whether by believer or disbeliever; sincere deeds are rewarded in the afterlife, others in this life.
rows.anchor: سواء كان عند الموت أو في الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised reward exceeds that of a bequest made during terminal illness, whose recompense might come in worldly life.
rows.anchor: أي مما لمن أوصى في مرض الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: End deeds by seeking forgiveness: even praised worship can produce self-admiration, and no one can render God His due, so servants must acknowledge shortcomings.
rows.anchor: ختام الأعمال بالاستغفار والاعتراف بالتقصير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's forgiveness covers sins and their effects until no blame or punishment remains; His mercy then adds generous honor and favor.
rows.anchor: أي بالغ الستر لأعيان الذنوب وآثارها

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The surah explains the Prophet's comprehensive supplication: make religion, worldly life, and afterlife good; make life increase good and death relief from evil.
rows.anchor: اللهم أصلح لي ديني الذي هو عصمة أمري وأصلح لي دنياي التي فيها معاشي وأصلح لي آخرتي التي إليها منقلبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's ending returns to its opening: encouragement to act and its reward recall the command to stand before God, while seeking forgiveness stresses the greatness of His station.
rows.anchor: رجع آخر السورة - بالترغيب في العمل وذكر جزائه - على أولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Surat al-Muddaththir aims to urge earnest warning of the ruinous abode for the arrogant, affirm resurrection to deniers, and signal good news to the mindful through God's clemency.
rows.anchor: مقصودها الجد والاجتهاد في الإنذار بدار البوار لأهل الاستكبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The title al-Muddaththir most clearly signals the surah's purpose, as reflection on the call, the one addressed, and its cause shows.
rows.anchor: واسمها المدثر أدل مافيها على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala calls God the highest sovereign and sole conqueror, whose existence and articulation blessings encompass righteous and wicked alike.
rows.anchor: الله } الملك الأعلى الواحد القهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's mercy gives His chosen people insight and success toward the lasting abode.
rows.anchor: الذي خص أهل أصفيائه بالاستبصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Muzzammil ends by giving good news to the perceptive after opening with strenuous service; al-Muddaththir opens with the messenger's warning to the lost.
rows.anchor: بالبشارة لأرباب البصارة بعدما بدئت بالاجتهاد في الخدمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mudaththir is one wrapped in a garment; dīthār is the outer garment over the shirt, as in the saying that the Ansar are the shirt and other people its outer garment.
rows.anchor: والدثار - بالكسر ما فوق الشعار من الثياب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root also evokes abundant wealth, a tree becoming leafy, and a bird tending its nest.
rows.anchor: والدثر : المار الكثير , ودثر الشجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address can signal either nearness or distance, but the context intends extreme nearness while the garment imagery partly veils it; the form suits a grave charge.
rows.anchor: التعبير بالأداة الصالحة للقرب والبعد يراد به غاية القرب بما عليه السياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The assimilated form suggests the garment did not cover the Prophet's whole body: covering the head and nearby body sufficed to focus the heart, and the assimilation suits wrapping.
rows.anchor: وكان الدثار لم يعم بدنه الشريف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because remaining wrapped confined and concealed him, he is commanded to rise with resolve and undertake the public reach required of a universal messenger.
rows.anchor: أمره صلى الله عليه وسلم بالقيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Warn everyone who can be warned, whether sunk in heedlessness or awake but veiled by distractions and fatigue.
rows.anchor: فأنذر من كان راقدا في غفلاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of warn is omitted to make its scope universal: everyone capable of disobedience and thus subject to warning.
rows.anchor: وحذف المفعول إشارة إلى عموم الإنذار

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The account says Gabriel's earlier revelation of “Read in your Lord's name” made Muhammad a prophet, while this revelation made him a messenger.
rows.anchor: ونحوها فكان بذلك نبيا ثم نزلت عليه هذه الآية فكان بها رسولا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: At Hira, Muhammad heard a voice, saw Gabriel enthroned between heaven and earth, was terrified, hurried home trembling, and asked to be covered and given cold water.
rows.anchor: فإذا جبريل عليه الصلاة والسلام جالس على عرش بين السماء والأرض

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: After the vision, the Prophet said that he feared for himself and asked his family to cover him and pour cold water over him.
rows.anchor: دثروني دثروني , لقد خشيت على نفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because warning confronts people with what they dislike, its burdens are either neglecting the command or demanding payment; the caller's aid is to magnify the sender and avoid wages.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الإنذار يتضمن مواجهة الناس بما يكرهون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Your Lord means the one who uniquely nurtures you; rise diligently and proclaim Him alone as greatest in speech and belief.
rows.anchor: أي المربي لك خاصة { فكبر * } أي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Magnifying God entails declaring Him free of partners and everything unworthy of Him, including association, division, supplication to others, and preoccupation with anything besides Him.
rows.anchor: وذلك تنزيهه عن الشرك أول كل شيء

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says the surahs' openings correspond: each addresses and honors the Prophet, commanding night standing in one and rising to warn in the other.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر بن الزبير : ملاءمتها لسورة المزمل واضحة

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr connects the commands to patience: al-Muzzammil says to endure what people say, and al-Muddaththir says to endure for the Lord; both follow one purpose.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر بن الزبير : ملاءمتها لسورة المزمل واضحة , واستفتاح السورتين من نمط واحد
